models_evaluated: seven LLMs (names not given in abstract), including quantized models, medically fine-tuned models, and an open-weight model

links.outcome: LLM performance under narrative perturbation probes versus clean baseline
links.effect: All models performed uniformly well at baseline; under narrative stress performance diverged sharply, with two stress-response phenotypes. Quantized models showed pseudonormalization (low flip rates hiding functional collapse).
links.quote: Under realistic narrative stress, performance diverged sharply, revealing two distinct stress-response phenotypes.

links.outcome: Whether clean benchmark accuracy reflects safety under realistic stress
links.effect: Models were uniformly good on clean baseline but diverged sharply under narrative stress, so benchmark accuracy did not reveal safety-relevant failures.
links.quote: Under clean baseline conditions, all models performed uniformly well.

links.outcome: Counterfactual fairness index across models, including effect of medical fine-tuning
links.effect: Medical supervised fine-tuning systematically degraded logical stability, fairness, and information extraction; fairness measured by counterfactual fairness index (CFI).
links.quote: Medical supervised fine-tuning systematically degraded logical stability, fairness, and information extraction.

unlisted_practices: Stress-audit framework using narrative perturbation probes with metrics (metabolic index, perturbation flip rate) for LLM safety evaluation
Assessing effects of model quantization on safety robustness
Comparing open-weight versus proprietary models on safety dimensions

screen.reason: The study develops and applies a benchmark stress-audit framework (AI-MASLD) using narrative perturbation probes to test the safety, fairness, and robustness of clinical LLMs. It evaluates model vulnerabilities rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
